recommendation: Keep the audit commit and do not restore a status/notTaken or status/taken matrix to current MedicationStatement. Future adherence explanatory improvements should be handled under newer adherence issues, not under FHIR-12470.
issue_request: FHIR-12470 was a Published Pharmacy change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking to repair MedicationStatement status plus notTaken/taken comments after STU3 element-name, datatype, and status-code changes and to revisit the combinations for active, completed, intended, stopped, on-hold, entered-in-error, and unknown.
initial_application: The Jira comments point to git-svn commit 3b901a8b986348f24b8043298ab9a1d288b13d19 as the original TR#12470 application. That commit updated MedicationStatement notes and spreadsheet source, renamed the notTaken binding/element to taken, made taken required with y | n | unk | na, adjusted the reason-not-taken invariant, and added a status-plus-taken interpretation table.
additional_context: Later Published R5 Pharmacy decisions superseded the old model. FHIR-19468 removed not-taken from MedicationStatement.status and directed taken/not-taken semantics to adherence; FHIR-19470 added MedicationStatement.adherence; FHIR-32060 changed status to recorded/entered-in-error/draft; FHIR-38682 renamed MedicationUsage back to MedicationStatement while retaining the redesign; and FHIR-39271 reaffirmed that status reflects the statement record while adherence reflects whether the medication is being taken. Related reconcile commits already exist on the combined branch for FHIR-19468, FHIR-19470, FHIR-32060, and FHIR-39271.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. MedicationStatement is active in source/fhir.ini, and the current source defines MedicationStatement.status as the recording status, MedicationStatement.adherence as taking/not-taking/adherence, effective[x] as the use or non-use interval, and current status/adherence code systems for the relevant states. The only remaining notTaken reference found is a historical [r2-renames] mapping, not current resource semantics.
